query: Consider the following context: The ability to endure extreme corrosion in challenging environments is reduced in stainless steel. This can be addressed by appropriate surface modification techniques to redefine the surface with the required properties. In that context, which method can be used for improved corrosion resistance, and why?

generation.hypothesis: Applying a chromium-based coating to stainless steel via electroplating will improve its corrosion resistance in challenging environments.
generation.material_initial_state: Austenitic stainless steel (SS304) in its annealed condition
generation.conditions: Coating thickness of 10 microns, applied at a current density of 10 mA/cm^2 for 2 hours
generation.structural_mediator: Chromium oxide layer formed on the surface
generation.mechanism: The chromium oxide layer acts as a barrier to corrosive species, reducing the diffusion of ions and thereby enhancing corrosion resistance
generation.predicted_outcome: A 30% reduction in corrosion rate, measured in mm/year, compared to uncoated stainless steel
generation.baseline: Uncoated SS304 in the same environment
generation.uncertainty: The actual improvement in corrosion resistance may vary depending on the specific coating parameters and environmental conditions

falsification_experiment.design: Immersion corrosion test in a 3.5% NaCl solution at 25°C
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the corrosion rate of the coated stainless steel is not at least 20% lower than the uncoated sample after 100 hours of exposure, the hypothesis is falsified
